literal: By nature quick-witted and eloquent, with a strong memory and wide learning; he valued guests and companions and excelled at discourse.
idiomatic: Quick-witted and eloquent, with a formidable memory and wide learning, he cherished guests and companions and excelled in debate.

literal: When he followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei westward in the migration, he was separately enfeoffed as Marquis of Ye County.
idiomatic: He followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei in the western migration and was separately enfeoffed as Marquis of Ye County.

literal: At the beginning of the Tianhe era of Zhou, he was advanced to General of Agile Cavalry and Director with the same ceremonial rank as the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: At the opening of Zhou's Tianhe era he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry with the ceremonial standing of the Three Excellencies.

literal: He served as governor of Xiong and Jiang provinces in succession, and in both posts earned a reputation for competence.
idiomatic: He governed Xiong and Jiang in turn, winning a name for competence in each.

literal: He inherited the title Duke of Pingyuan.
idiomatic: He inherited the ducal title of Pingyuan.

literal: He died; his son Chi succeeded.
idiomatic: When he died, his son Chi succeeded him.

literal: Chi, great-grandson of You
idiomatic: Chi, a great-grandson of You

literal: Chi, styled Zhongguang, was clever and quick, handsome in bearing, had read widely among the classics, and was also skilled in martial arts.
idiomatic: Chi, styled Zhongguang, was clever and handsome, had dipped into many books, and was skilled in arms as well.

literal: At the beginning of the Jiande era, Emperor Wu of Zhou, honoring the Way, sought men versed in both the classics and histories to serve as scholars of the Passage Hall; Chi was chosen.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou, at the start of Jiande, sought scholars versed in classics and histories for the Passage Hall, Chi was among those chosen.

literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was prime minister, he was raised from Superior Gentleman of the Imperial Rectitude to Merit Officer in the Chancellor's Office, given the grand commandant rank, enfeoffed as Viscount of Yangping, and moved to Junior Grand Master of the Lesser Earl.
idiomatic: When Wen of Sui was still prime minister, Chi rose from Superior Gentleman of the Imperial Rectitude to merit officer in the chancellor's office, was made grand commandant, enfeoffed Viscount of Yangping, and promoted to junior grand master of the lesser earl.

literal: For suppressing Prince of Qi Wang Qian, he was awarded the ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: For helping crush Wang Qian, Prince of Qi, he received the ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

literal: When the emperor received the abdication, Chi led the officials in first entering the cleared palace; he was at once made Palace Attendant of the Inner Secretariat and superior ceremonial peer of the Three Excellencies, acting as Right Vice Heir Apparent of the Eastern Palace, moving in and out of both palaces and greatly trusted.
idiomatic: At the founding of Sui, Chi led the officials into the cleared palace first and was made palace attendant of the inner secretariat with superior ceremonial rank, acting right vice heir apparent of the eastern palace—trusted in both courts.

literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of Ceremonies, his fief changed to Viscount of Raoyang, advanced to Director with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, and transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.
idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of ceremonies, had his fief changed to Raoyang, was given director's ceremonial rank, and became vice minister of personnel.

literal: In the Daye era he held the posts of Minister of Justice and Minister of Revenue in succession.
idiomatic: Under Daye he served in turn as minister of justice and minister of revenue.

literal: When Tuyuhun raided Zhangye, Chi was ordered to strike them and pursued them to Qinghai; for his merit he was given the title Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Silver Seal.
idiomatic: When Tuyuhun raided Zhangye, Chi pursued them to Qinghai and, for his merit, was made grand master of splendid brightness with silver seal.

literal: In the sixth year the emperor visited the Jiangdu Palace and left Chi at the eastern capital as commandant, acting as Left Commander of the Waiting Guard.
idiomatic: In year six the emperor went to the Jiangdu palace and left Chi at the eastern capital as commandant, acting left commander of the waiting guard.

literal: He died in office; his posthumous title was Jing.
idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously titled Jing.

literal: His son Anshi was an attendant for miscellaneous matters.
idiomatic: His son Anshi served as attendant for miscellaneous matters.

literal: Sheng, younger brother of Chi.
idiomatic: Chi had a younger brother, Sheng.

literal: Sheng, younger brother of Chi
idiomatic: Sheng, younger brother of Chi

literal: Sheng, styled Jisheng, was quick and penetrating by nature, had dipped into written records, was skilled at archery and shooting, and was more agile than other men.
idiomatic: Sheng, styled Jisheng, was quick and keen, had some schooling, excelled at archery, and moved with uncanny agility.

literal: At eighteen he entered Zhou's service as Superior Gentleman of the Palace Guards.
idiomatic: At eighteen he entered Zhou's service as superior gentleman of the palace guards.

literal: At first he was not yet known; only Emperor Wen of Sui, on a single meeting, was deeply struck and said to him:
idiomatic: At first he was unknown—until Emperor Wen of Sui met him once and was deeply struck, saying:

literal: "Changsun's martial skill surpasses the crowd, and he has many singular stratagems.
idiomatic: "Changsun's martial skill surpasses the crowd, and he holds many singular stratagems.

literal: The famous general of later days—will it not be this man?"
idiomatic: The famous general of later days—will it not be this man?"

literal: When the Türk Qaghan Shetu sought marriage, Zhou gave him the daughter of Prince Zhao of Zhao as wife.
idiomatic: When the Türk qaghan Shetu sought a marriage alliance, Zhou gave him the daughter of Prince Zhao.

literal: Zhou and Shetu each boasted against the other and chose the finest warriors to serve as envoys; Sheng was therefore sent as deputy to the Duke of Runan, Yuwen Shenqing, to escort the Princess of a Thousand Gold to his camp.
idiomatic: Zhou and Shetu each boasted their valor and picked the finest warriors as envoys; Sheng was sent as deputy to Duke of Runan Yuwen Shenqing to escort the Princess of a Thousand Gold to Shetu's camp.

literal: Envoys before and after numbered several tens; Shetu was mostly discourteous to them, but he alone favored Sheng, hunted with him constantly, and kept him a full year.
idiomatic: Dozens of envoys came and went; Shetu treated most discourteously, but favored Sheng alone, hunted with him constantly, and kept him a full year.

literal: Once two eagles flew up fighting over meat; he therefore gave Sheng two arrows and asked him to shoot them down.
idiomatic: Once two eagles fought in the air over meat; Shetu gave Sheng two arrows and asked him to bring them down.

literal: Sheng galloped up; when he met the eagles grappling each other, he loosed one shaft and pierced both.
idiomatic: Sheng galloped up, found the eagles locked together, and dropped them both with a single shot.

literal: Shetu was pleased and ordered all his younger kinsmen and nobles to befriend Sheng, hoping to draw near him and learn archery.
idiomatic: Delighted, Shetu had his younger kinsmen and nobles befriend Sheng so they might learn archery from him.

literal: His younger brother Chuluohou, titled Tuli She, was especially beloved by the people and was envied by Shetu; he secretly entrusted his heart to Sheng and secretly allied with him.
idiomatic: His younger brother Chuluohou, titled Tuli She, was especially beloved by the people and envied by Shetu; he secretly entrusted himself to Sheng and made a hidden alliance.

literal: Sheng hunted with him and thereby surveyed the mountains and rivers, the terrain, and the strength of the tribes.
idiomatic: Sheng hunted with him and surveyed mountains, rivers, terrain, and tribal strength.

literal: He came to know them all thoroughly.
idiomatic: He came to know them all thoroughly.

literal: On his return he was made Commandant of the Imperial Carriage.
idiomatic: On his return he was made commandant of the imperial carriage.

literal: In the first year of Kaihuang, Shetu said:
idiomatic: In Kaihuang's first year Shetu said:

literal: "I am kin to the house of Zhou.
idiomatic: "I am kin to the house of Zhou.

literal: Now the Duke of Sui has set himself up and I cannot control him—what face have I to show the kehuden!"
idiomatic: Now the Duke of Sui has set himself up and I cannot control him—what face have I to show the kehuden!"

literal: He therefore joined Gao Baoning in attacking and taking Linyu Fort, rallied the tribal chiefs of the various divisions, and plotted a joint southern invasion.
idiomatic: He joined Gao Baoning in taking Linyu Fort, rallied the tribal chiefs, and plotted a joint invasion of the south.

literal: The emperor had newly taken the throne and was therefore greatly afraid; he repaired the Long Wall and sent troops to garrison the northern border.
idiomatic: Wen had only just taken the throne and was greatly alarmed; he repaired the Long Wall and sent troops to the northern marches.

literal: He ordered Yin Shou to garrison Youzhou and Yu Qingze to garrison Bingzhou, stationing troops as a precaution.
idiomatic: He ordered Yin Shou to hold Youzhou and Yu Qingze to hold Bingzhou, with troops stationed as a precaution.

literal: Sheng had long known that Shetu, Dianjue, Abo, Tuli, and other uncles, nephews, and brothers each commanded strong armies, all styled qaghan, holding the four quarters—harboring suspicion within while showing harmony without—hard to conquer by force, easy to sunder by division.
idiomatic: Sheng had long known that Shetu, Dianjue, Abo, Tuli, and other uncles and brothers each commanded strong armies, all styled qaghan and holding the four quarters—suspicious within, harmonious without—hard to conquer by force, easy to split by intrigue.

literal: He therefore submitted a memorial saying:
idiomatic: He therefore memorialized:

literal: "Your servant, at the end of Zhou, was honored to serve as envoy abroad; the Türks' rises and falls are what I know in detail.
idiomatic: "At the end of Zhou your servant was honored to serve abroad; the Türks' rises and falls I know in detail.

literal: Dianjue toward Shetu has the stronger army but the lower rank; outwardly they are joined in name, but inwardly the rift is already plain—if their passions are stirred, they will surely fight each other.
idiomatic: Dianjue toward Shetu has the stronger army but the lower rank; joined in name outwardly, their rift is already plain—stir their passions and they will fight each other.

literal: Chuluohou is Shetu's younger brother—cunning and numerous in followers but weak in power; he curries the people's hearts and the nation loves him, and therefore Shetu envies him.
idiomatic: Chuluohou is Shetu's younger brother—cunning, weak in power, beloved of the people, and therefore envied by Shetu.

literal: Abo is irresolute, caught between them; he fears Shetu much, is pulled along by him, follows only the strong, and has no settled heart.
idiomatic: Abo wavers between them, fears Shetu, is pulled along by him, follows only the strong, and has no settled heart.

literal: One should befriend the distant and attack the near, divide the strong and unite the weak.
idiomatic: Befriend the distant, attack the near; divide the strong, unite the weak.

literal: Send envoys to Dianjue and persuade Abo to join him, and Shetu will turn his army to guard the western lands himself.
idiomatic: Send envoys to Dianjue and win Abo to him, and Shetu will turn his army to guard the west himself.

literal: Also draw in Chuluohou and send him to link with Xi and Qi, and Shetu will divide his host and return to guard the eastern quarter.
idiomatic: Draw in Chuluohou and link him with Xi and Qi, and Shetu will divide his host to guard the east.

literal: Suspicion at the tail, estrangement at the heart—after a dozen years or so, strike when the chance appears, and in one move you may empty their state."
idiomatic: Suspicion at the tail, estrangement at the heart—after a dozen years strike when chance appears, and in one move you may empty their state."

literal: The emperor, on reading the memorial, was greatly pleased and summoned him to speak.
idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial with delight and summoned him to speak.

literal: Sheng set forth the situation with his mouth and drew the mountains and rivers with his hand, writing out their strengths and weaknesses as if they lay in his palm.
idiomatic: Sheng described the situation aloud and sketched mountains and rivers with his hand, laying out strength and weakness as if on his palm.

literal: The emperor sighed in deep admiration and adopted it all.
idiomatic: The emperor sighed in admiration and adopted it all.

literal: He therefore sent the Grand Master of the Stud Yuan Hui by the Yiwu route with envoys to Dianjue, bestowing a wolf-head banner and falsely showing deep respect.
idiomatic: He sent Grand Master of the Stud Yuan Hui by the Yiwu route to Dianjue with a wolf-head banner and feigned deep respect.

literal: When Dianjue's envoy came, he was lodged above Shetu's envoy.
idiomatic: When Dianjue's envoy arrived, he was lodged above Shetu's envoy.

literal: Once the stratagem of division was set in motion, they truly became mutually suspicious.
idiomatic: Once the stratagem of division was set in motion, they truly became mutually suspicious.

literal: Sheng was made General of the Chariots and Cavalry and sent out by the Yellow Dragon route, bearing worn gifts for Xi, Qi, Khitan, and others, sent as guides, and reached Chuluohou's camp, where he laid out his inner thoughts deeply and enticed him to submit inwardly.
idiomatic: Sheng was made general of chariots and cavalry and sent by the Yellow Dragon route with worn gifts for Xi, Qi, Khitan, and others as guides; he reached Chuluohou, won his confidence, and enticed him to submit.

literal: In the second year Shetu, styled at four hundred thousand horsemen, entered from Lanzhou as far as Zhoupan and broke the army of Daxi Changru.
idiomatic: In the second year Shetu, claiming four hundred thousand horsemen, entered from Lanzhou to Zhoupan and broke Daxi Changru's army.

literal: He wished to press farther south, but Dianjue would not follow and led his troops away.
idiomatic: He wished to press farther south, but Dianjue refused and led his troops away.

literal: At that time Sheng also persuaded Ran'gan to falsely report to Shetu:
idiomatic: At that time Sheng also persuaded Ran'gan to falsely report to Shetu:

literal: "The Tiele and others have rebelled and mean to strike your camp."
idiomatic: "The Tiele and others have rebelled and mean to strike your camp."

literal: Shetu was therefore afraid and turned his army back beyond the border.
idiomatic: Shetu was afraid and turned his army back beyond the border.

literal: Several years later the Türks invaded in force; eight route marshals were sent out to resist.
idiomatic: Several years later the Türks invaded in force and eight route marshals were sent to resist.

literal: Abo reached Liangzhou and fought Dou Rongding; the enemy leaders were repeatedly defeated.
idiomatic: Abo reached Liangzhou and fought Dou Rongding; the enemy leaders were repeatedly defeated.

literal: At that time Sheng was a subordinate general and sent word to him:
idiomatic: At that time Sheng was a subordinate general and sent word to him:

literal: "Whenever Shetu comes, battle always ends in great victory.
idiomatic: "Whenever Shetu comes, battle always ends in great victory.

literal: Abo has only just entered and at once suffers defeat—this is the Türks' shame.
idiomatic: Abo has only just entered and at once suffers defeat—this is the Türks' shame.

literal: Moreover Shetu and Abo were originally equal in military strength; now Shetu wins day by day and is exalted by the masses, while Abo fares ill and brings disgrace on the state.
idiomatic: Moreover Shetu and Abo were originally equal in strength; now Shetu wins day by day and is exalted by the masses, while Abo fares ill and brings disgrace on the state.

literal: Shetu will surely use this to lay the blame on Abo and accomplish his long-held plan to destroy the northern camp."
idiomatic: Shetu will surely use this to lay the blame on Abo and accomplish his long-held plan to destroy the northern camp."

literal: When Abo's envoy arrived, Sheng also said to him:
idiomatic: When Abo's envoy arrived, Sheng also said to him:

literal: "Now Datou is allied with Sui, and Shetu cannot control him.
idiomatic: "Now Datou is allied with Sui, and Shetu cannot control him.

literal: Why does the qaghan not attach himself to the Son of Heaven, join with Datou, and combine into strength?
idiomatic: Why does the qaghan not attach himself to the Son of Heaven, join with Datou, and combine into strength?

literal: This is the plan of perfect safety.
idiomatic: This is the plan of perfect safety.

literal: Will you rather lose your army, bear guilt, return to Shetu, and suffer his slaughter and humiliation!"
idiomatic: Will you rather lose your army, bear guilt, return to Shetu, and suffer his slaughter and humiliation!"

literal: Abo accepted this and therefore remained beyond the border.
idiomatic: Abo accepted this and remained beyond the border.

literal: Abo won repeatedly and his power grew ever stronger.
idiomatic: Abo won again and again, and his power grew ever stronger.

literal: Shetu again sent envoys with tribute; the princess herself asked to change her surname and begged to be made the emperor's daughter, and the emperor assented.
idiomatic: Shetu again sent tribute; the princess asked to take the emperor's surname and become his daughter, and the emperor assented.

literal: In the fourth year Sheng was sent as deputy to Yu Qingze on a mission to Shetu; the princess was given the surname Yang and her fief changed to Princess of Great Righteousness.
idiomatic: In the fourth year Sheng went as deputy to Yu Qingze to Shetu; the princess was given the surname Yang and enfeoffed as Princess of Great Righteousness.

literal: Shetu received the edict but refused to rise and bow.
idiomatic: Shetu received the edict but refused to rise and bow.

literal: Sheng advanced and said:
idiomatic: Sheng stepped forward and said:

literal: "Türks and Sui are both great states of the Son of Heaven; if the qaghan does not rise, how dare I disobey his will.
idiomatic: "Türks and Sui are both great powers of the Son of Heaven; if the qaghan does not rise, how dare I disobey his will.

literal: But the kehuden is the emperor's daughter—then the qaghan is the great son-in-law of Great Sui; how can he fail to respect his wife's father-in-law?"
idiomatic: But the kehuden is the emperor's daughter—then the qaghan is Great Sui's son-in-law; how can he fail to respect his wife's father-in-law?"

literal: Shetu laughed and said to his nobles, "One must bow to the wife's father-in-law."
idiomatic: Shetu laughed and told his nobles, "One must bow to the wife's father-in-law."

literal: He then bowed and received the edict.
idiomatic: He then bowed and received the edict.

literal: In the seventh year Shetu died; Sheng was sent bearing credentials to invest his younger brother Chuluohou as Mohe Qaghan and his son Yonglu as Yehu Qaghan.
idiomatic: In the seventh year Shetu died; Sheng was sent with credentials to invest his younger brother Chuluohou as Mohe Qaghan and his son Yonglu as Yehu Qaghan.

literal: Chuluohou, through Sheng, memorialized:
idiomatic: Chuluohou, through Sheng, memorialized:

literal: "Abo was destroyed by Heaven and is in the mountain valleys with five or six thousand horsemen—he should be taken and presented."
idiomatic: "Abo was destroyed by Heaven and is in the mountain valleys with five or six thousand horsemen—he should be taken and presented."

literal: At that time civil and military officials were summoned to deliberate.
idiomatic: Civil and military officials were summoned to deliberate.

literal: Yue'an Xi Yuanxie of the Western Regions said:
idiomatic: Yue'an Xi Yuanxie of the Western Regions said:

literal: "Please go there and take his head to punish his wickedness."
idiomatic: "Please go there and take his head to punish his wickedness."

literal: Duke of Wuyang Li Chong asked to bring him alive into court and display the execution to the people.
idiomatic: Duke of Wuyang Li Chong asked to bring him alive into court and display the execution to the people.

literal: Better to let both survive."
idiomatic: Better to let both survive."

literal: The emperor said, "Good."
idiomatic: The emperor said, "Good."

literal: In the eighth year Chuluohou died; Sheng was sent to offer condolences and also bore treasure vessels presented by Chen to bestow on Yonglu.
idiomatic: In the eighth year Chuluohou died; Sheng was sent to mourn him and bore treasure vessels Chen had presented, to bestow on Yonglu.

literal: In the thirteenth year the exiled Yang Qin fled into the Türks and falsely said that Duke of Peng Liu Chang together with a daughter of the Yuwen clan plotted rebellion against Sui, sending him to secretly inform the princess.
idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the exile Yang Qin fled to the Türks and falsely claimed that Duke of Peng Liu Chang and a Yuwen daughter plotted against Sui, sending him to secretly inform the princess.

literal: Yonglu believed it and therefore ceased paying tribute.
idiomatic: Yonglu believed it and stopped sending tribute.

literal: Sheng was again sent on mission to observe subtly.
idiomatic: Sheng was again sent on mission to observe subtly.

literal: The princess saw Sheng with insolent speech and also sent her private Türk An Suijia together with Qin to plot, stirring Yonglu.
idiomatic: The princess saw Sheng with insolent speech and also sent her private Turk An Suijia with Qin to plot, stirring Yonglu.

literal: Sheng returned and memorialized the facts.
idiomatic: Sheng returned and memorialized the facts.
